A1.justification: Both PDFs contain the same SocialNav research work and complete, readable appendices A–C. Pages 2–19 have identical extracted text and rendered content; first-page differences are confined to the author list and arXiv stamp.

before.justification: v1 reports original open-loop, simulated closed-loop, and real-world navigation experiments, plus data/training ablations and an appendix reward ablation (Tables 1–4, 8–9).

after.justification: v2 retains the same original navigation experiments, ablations, and qualitative results in the main text and appendices.

M1.justification: The VLM Brain, flow-matching Action Expert, three-stage training pipeline, and SAFE-GRPO procedure and rewards are identical (Section 4 and Appendix B).

E1.justification: Both versions use the same SocNav training data, CityWalker benchmark, nine-scene SocNav benchmark, real-world environments, and supplementary test scenarios.

E2.justification: Comparator membership is unchanged: GNM, ViNT, NoMaD, and CityWalker retain their corresponding variants in Tables 1–3 and 9. The Qwen2.5-VL traversability comparison in Figure 6 is also identical.

E3.justification: Training settings, model configurations, metrics, benchmark sampling, pedestrian simulation, and the 20 trials per real-world environment remain unchanged (Sections 3.2 and 5; Appendices A.4 and B).

E4.justification: The data-composition and training-stage ablations in Table 4, social-reward ablation in Table 8, and qualitative trajectory, traversability, and reasoning analyses are identical.

E5.justification: Both retain the same point estimates and trial success counts. Neither adds seed information, confidence intervals, significance tests, or other uncertainty reporting.

E6.justification: All numerical entries and qualitative findings are unchanged, including appendix results. For example, Table 2 retains SocialNav's SR 86.1, DCR 82.5, and TCR 82.9, while Table 3 retains average real-world SR 85.0.

T1.justification: The navigation formulation, flow-policy equations, metric definitions, trajectory-generation mathematics, and reward formulas are identical throughout the main text and appendices.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same claims about SocialNav, SAFE-GRPO, the dataset and benchmark, and improved navigation and social compliance.

C2.justification: Interpretations of cognitive priors and reinforcement learning, the social-compliance versus path-efficiency tradeoff, and limitations concerning semantic traversability and handcrafted rewards are unchanged.

D1.justification: Implementation details, hyperparameters, hardware, data-generation and annotation instructions, prompt template, and project/resource links are unchanged. The updated arXiv version link introduces no reproducibility information.

R1.justification: The related-work discussion, all 51 bibliography entries, and positioning relative to navigation models and flow-based reinforcement learning are identical.

P1.justification: v2 adds Ning Guo to the author list and updates the arXiv version/date stamp. Scientific prose, terminology, section organization, and appendix structure remain unchanged.

P2.justification: The third author row is respaced to accommodate the added author, and the marginal arXiv stamp changes. All figures, tables, captions, and remaining page layouts are unchanged.

improvement.justification: The revision changes authorship presentation and version information without changing the scientific argument, empirical evidence, limitations, or reproducibility details, including the appendices. These changes establish no meaningful difference in overall paper quality.
